summary: The United States declared a zero-tolerance policy on mine placement in the Strait of Hormuz, announcing all mines have been cleared and threatening immediate destruction of any vessel laying new mines, while also monitoring Iranian nuclear sites. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu confirmed President Trump approved intensifying the economic siege on Iran by targeting its enablers. Meanwhile, an Iranian plot to assassinate Yair Netanyahu in Miami was foiled in December, prompting his urgent return to Israel.
key_points: Trump announced all mines removed from Strait of Hormuz international waters and warned any new mine placement will be systematically destroyed, with Space Force monitoring the strait and destroyed nuclear sites. (Source: @shin_persian/9102)

Netanyahu stated Trump strongly reconfirmed intensifying economic siege on Iran by targeting those assisting the regime, while expressing doubt about reaching a nuclear deal. (Source: @SharghDaily/180185)
Israeli intelligence uncovered an Iranian cell conducting surveillance on Yair Netanyahu in Miami in December, leading to his immediate evacuation and return to Israel. (Source: @almogboker78/18060)
IDF struck multiple locations in southern Lebanon overnight including Kfar Roumman, Ali Taher, Al-Mansouri, Sarafand, and Al-Qantara. (Source: @yediotnews25/134324)

IAF bombed a Hamas ambush position and weapons storage in Jabalia, northern Gaza, 50 meters from the Yellow Line, killing several operatives; site was 70m from Kamal Adwan Hospital and 170m from a school. (Source: @manniefabian/59044)
Palestinian media reported one dead and several injured in an Israeli strike on a tent in Khan Younis, southern Gaza. (Source: @manniefabian/59043)
Qatar's LNG exports dropped 96% after effective closure of Strait of Hormuz, with only 18 shipments versus 509 previously, losing nearly $24 billion in revenue. (Source: @naya_foriraq/88539)
IRGC announced agreement with Oman on respective shares of Strait of Hormuz waters and revenues. (Source: @naya_foriraq/88553)

sections.executive_summary: The United States declared a zero-tolerance policy on mine placement in the Strait of Hormuz, announcing all mines have been cleared and threatening immediate destruction of any vessel laying new mines, while also monitoring Iranian nuclear sites. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu confirmed President Trump approved intensifying the economic siege on Iran by targeting its enablers. Meanwhile, an Iranian plot to assassinate Yair Netanyahu in Miami was foiled in December, prompting his urgent return to Israel.

points: Iranian Parliament Speaker Qalibaf threatened confrontation with the United States 'with the sword of power' if demands are not met, stating the distance between diplomatic conflict and military confrontation is short and 'our fingers are on the trigger.' (Source: @naya_foriraq/88550)

The IRGC announced an agreement with Oman on each side's share of Strait of Hormuz waters and revenue shares, indicating bilateral coordination on the strategic waterway. (Source: @naya_foriraq/88553)

US authorities are investigating an Iranian hack of a water utility technology company's data, per Reuters, highlighting ongoing cyber threats to critical infrastructure. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/387002)

An Iranian cell conducted surveillance on Yair Netanyahu's Miami residence and daily routine in December, prompting an urgent US-Israeli response and his immediate evacuation to Israel. (Source: @almogboker78/18060)

President Trump declared all mines removed from international waters of the Strait of Hormuz, warned any new mine placement will be 'immediately and systematically destroyed,' and stated Space Force is watching 'every square inch' of the strait along with 'Pickaxe Mountain and the already destroyed three other nuclear sites.' (Source: @shin_persian/9102)

The Wall Street Journal noted nearly six months after Trump's promised six-week timeline, engagement with Iran continues without a clear end, indicating prolonged diplomatic-military tension. (Source: @kianmeli1/91111)

Prime Minister Netanyahu revealed he proposed to Trump intensifying the economic siege on Iran by targeting those assisting the regime, and Trump 'very very very strongly' reconfirmed this decision yesterday. (Source: @SharghDaily/180185)

IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir met with US Air Force Commander Gen. Kenneth Wilsbach and IAF Commander Maj. Gen. Omer Tishler to discuss regional assessment, lessons from joint operations, and future cooperation areas. (Source: @yediotnews25/134332)
IDF struck multiple sites in southern Lebanon overnight including Kfar Roumman, Ali Taher, Al-Mansouri, Sarafand, and Al-Qantara, according to Lebanese reports. (Source: @yediotnews25/134324)

IAF bombed a Hamas facility in Jabalia, northern Gaza, serving as an 'ambush position' and weapons storage, located 50 meters from the IDF 'Yellow Line,' 70 meters from Kamal Adwan Hospital, and 170 meters from a school; several Hamas operatives killed. (Source: @manniefabian/59044)
Chief of Staff Zamir visited Gaza Strip forces and held a situation assessment with sector commanders, following response strikes on incendiary kites. (Source: @inon_yttach/9946)
A false rocket alert triggered in the Home Front Command app for Kibbutz Alumim area was identified as a false alarm with no security threat. (Source: @inon_yttach/9952)

IAF struck a Hamas ambush position and weapons storage in Jabalia, northern Gaza, 50 meters from the IDF 'Yellow Line,' killing several operatives; the site was 70 meters from Kamal Adwan Hospital and 170 meters from a school. (Source: @manniefabian/59044)
Palestinian media reported one dead and several injured in an Israeli strike targeting a tent in Khan Younis, southern Gaza; the military has not commented. (Source: @manniefabian/59043)
IDF Chief of Staff Zamir visited fighting forces in Gaza and conducted a situation assessment with commanders in the sector. (Source: @inon_yttach/9946)
A false rocket alert for Kibbutz Alumim area was issued via the Home Front Command app, later confirmed as a false identification with no security event. (Source: @inon_yttach/9952)
IDF observers in Gaza Division were described by the Chief of Staff as 'our eyes — the first to identify infiltration threats and activate forces to thwart them.' (Source: @idf_telegram/24986)
IDF conducted overnight strikes in southern Lebanon hitting Kfar Roumman, Ali Taher, Al-Mansouri, Sarafand, and Al-Qantara, per Lebanese reports. (Source: @yediotnews25/134324)

US Ambassador to Lebanon Michelle Sison stated the US is ready to negotiate with Hezbollah 'if they have something to offer,' while noting Lebanon-Israel negotiations have not stopped and Rome talks are technical with no specific timeline. (Source: @SharghDaily/180178)
Drone flights were reported along the Lebanese coast from Al-Ula to Khaldeh, indicating aerial surveillance or operational activity. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/387007)
Netanyahu emphasized the challenge in Lebanon 'has not ended' and Israel is determined to finish challenges in Gaza, Lebanon, and other arenas. (Source: @SharghDaily/180185)

Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council head Faiq Zidan met with US Embassy Chargé d'Affaires Joshua Harris in Baghdad after returning from Iran, discussing judicial measures after the international coalition mission ends September 30, including parties bearing arms contrary to the constitution. (Source: @SharghDaily/180176)

Qatar's LNG exports plummeted 96% after effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, with only 18 shipments compared to 509 the previous year, resulting in nearly $24 billion in lost gas revenue. (Source: @naya_foriraq/88539)
Oil tanker SAYA, managed by a Chinese company, transited the Strait of Hormuz en route to Imam Khomeini port after returning from India. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/386992)
IRGC announced agreement with Oman on respective shares of Strait of Hormuz waters and revenue shares. (Source: @naya_foriraq/88553)

US tanker tracking shows multiple KC-46A and KC-135R movements in the region, including flights from Europe to the Middle East, suggesting heightened aerial refueling activity. (Source: @shin_persian/9113)

sections.threat_assessment: The convergence of US declaratory policy on Hormuz mine clearance and nuclear site monitoring, coupled with Netanyahu's confirmation of an intensified economic siege on Iran's enablers, signals a coordinated pressure campaign that Tehran perceives as an existential threat. Qalibaf's explicit warning that the distance between diplomatic and military confrontation is short, combined with the foiled assassination plot against the Prime Minister's son, indicates Iranian willingness to escalate asymmetrically. Meanwhile, continued IDF strikes in Lebanon and Gaza, including precision targeting near sensitive sites, risk triggering broader regional responses from Hezbollah and Hamas. The collapse of Qatar's LNG exports demonstrates the economic fragility of Gulf energy routes under current tensions.
sections.regional_response: Oman's agreement with the IRGC on Hormuz revenue sharing suggests Gulf states are hedging by engaging Iran diplomatically while the US pursues maximum pressure. The US Ambassador's conditional offer to negotiate with Hezbollah reflects a dual-track approach of military support for Israel alongside diplomatic off-ramps. Iraq's judicial discussions with the US post-Iran visit reveal Baghdad's attempt to balance between Tehran and Washington ahead of the coalition withdrawal deadline. Qatar's catastrophic LNG revenue loss may push Doha toward mediation efforts to reopen Hormuz, while increased US tanker movements signal sustained military readiness.
sections.intelligence_notes: The specificity of Trump's Truth Social statement — naming 'Pickaxe Mountain' and 'three other nuclear sites already destroyed' — suggests either operational disclosure or psychological warfare; verification of physical damage to Iranian nuclear facilities is required. The Miami assassination plot's December timeline implies Iranian operational patience and reach into the US homeland, raising concerns about other dormant cells. The Jabalia strike's proximity to a hospital and school (70m and 170m) will likely generate international scrutiny and potential war crimes allegations, complicating Israel's legal position. False rocket alerts in Alumim indicate either sensor spoofing or heightened IDF alert posture amid multi-front tensions.
